statement: You receive a sorted row of integers and a target integer. Print the lower bound of the target: the smallest index whose value is greater than or equal to the target. If no such index exists, print n, the length of the row. Use binary search; a linear scan does the same job too slowly to count here.
constraints: The row is sorted ascending and may contain duplicates.

example.why: Index 1 holds the first value that is at least 4; index 0 holds 2, which is below.

hint: Remember mid as the best answer whenever its value passes the test, then keep hunting strictly left of it.
mistake: Returning on the first equality - with duplicates the first passing index may sit further left than the first hit.
